name: Air Fryer BBQ Shrimp Skewers with Rice and Sweetcorn

components.name: BBQ Shrimp Skewers

ingredients.name: Raw large shrimp peeled and deveined, shells discarded
Prepared honey barbecue sauce, no alcohol

steps: Toss shrimp with measured oil, paprika and salt. Thread shrimp onto air-fryer-safe metal skewers, or cook loose in a basket when skewers cannot fit.
Brush half of the measured barbecue sauce over shrimp and set the other half aside clean before it touches raw seafood.
Air fry at 190 C for 6-10 minutes, turning once and applying a little of the reserved CLEAN sauce, until shrimp reach 63 C. If any sauce has touched raw shrimp, cook it thoroughly before serving.
Serve or pack four portions of rice, shrimp and corn salad. Keep salad cool, and reheat shrimp only briefly to prevent rubbery texture.

components.name: Basmati Rice
steps: Rinse the rice and cook covered using 510 ml of water. Rest off heat, then cool rapidly for meal prep.

components.name: Sweetcorn & Pepper Salad
steps: Combine sweetcorn, diced peppers, onion, lime and coriander into a separate salad.

notes: Draft — needs Mirna review: not kitchen-tested yet; macros and cooked yields are estimates.
Published H-E-B air-fried barbecue shrimp skewers used for core technique. Rice and corn salad are quantified UNHANGRY sides.
Planning: SECONDARY STOVETOP rice. Do not use wooden skewers that exceed air fryer capacity.
Freezer: cooked shrimp and rice can freeze, but corn and pepper salad is better fresh
Dietary: Shellfish; verify BBQ sauce is halal/alcohol-free and does not contain wheat/soy allergens.

Refrigerate within 2 hours (1 hour above 32°C) in shallow containers at 4°C or colder, for 3–4 days at most, and follow the shorter seafood limit above. Cook fish and shellfish to 63°C and reheat leftovers to at least 74°C.

flags.shelfLife: Shrimp — plan for days 1-3; the corn salad is better fresh.

preservationAndReheating: Refrigerate cooked food promptly in shallow covered containers. Target within 2 hours, or 1 hour when ambient temperature exceeds 32 C.
Refrigerate at 4 C or below for 3-4 days maximum; for many fish and shrimp dishes, prioritize eating within 1-2 days for quality and freeze later-week cooked portions promptly.

Cook fish and crustaceans to 63 C (145 F) or applicable local food-safety standard, and reheat cooked leftovers to 74 C. For crab cakes containing egg binder and purchased cooked crab, reheat to 74 C.
When recipe includes rice, cool rapidly and refrigerate promptly; do not leave cooked rice at room temperature.
Freeze in suitable airtight food-safe containers. Defrost in refrigerator, not on counter. Re-crisp breading in an air fryer when possible.
Do not freeze fresh avocado, uncooked tomato/cucumber/cabbage salad, or mayonnaise/yogurt-based dressing unless kitchen-tested separately.
Freezer suitability here describes expected eating quality, not laboratory validated shelf life.
